text: Found it: `Interval.fromISO` in src/interval.js calls `DateTime.fromISO` on both halves, so with `Settings.throwOnInvalid = true` an InvalidDateTimeError is thrown before the code can fall back to parsing the other half as a Duration (and before `Interval.invalid` can throw the proper InvalidIntervalError). A subagent is applying the fix and running the full test suite; ETA ~8 min.

`NaN`. In `parseDigits` (src/impl/digits.js:50), `parseInt(str, 10)` is NaN for such input, so it falls into the fallback branch: it builds `value = ""` and the loop appends nothing (no char matches the hanidec regex or any of the `numberingSystemsUTF16` ranges), then `parseInt("", 10)` returns `NaN`. So the function returns `NaN` (not 0, not `""`).

It returns `[null, {}]` — i.e. the raw match is `null` (what `String.prototype.match` returns on no match) paired with an empty object for the parsed token values (src/impl/tokenParser.js:264-266). The caller at line 390 destructures this as `[rawMatches, matches]`, and the `null` raw match is what makes the parse fail (e.g. `DateTime.fromFormat` returns an invalid DateTime with reason "unparsable").

It returns an `Invalid` object (from src/impl/invalid.js) describing the problem, not a boolean. In `hasInvalidWeekData` (src/impl/conversions.js:100-112), `validYear = isInteger(obj.weekYear)` is false, so the first branch runs: `return unitOutOfRange("weekYear", obj.weekYear)`, i.e. `new Invalid("unit out of range", \`you specified ${obj.weekYear} (of type ${typeof obj.weekYear}) as a weekYear, which is invalid\`)`. (Only when all three checks pass does it return `false`.)

Fixed and verified. `Interval.fromISO` now wraps each `DateTime.fromISO` call in try/catch, so when `Settings.throwOnInvalid` is true a thrown InvalidDateTimeError is treated as "that half isn't a DateTime", letting the code fall through to the Duration interpretation and finally to `Interval.invalid(...)` (which throws InvalidIntervalError). Verified with throwOnInvalid on: start/duration, duration/end and start/end strings all return valid Intervals, and `"bad"` / `"foo/bar"` throw InvalidIntervalError. `npx jest test/interval` is 127/127 green; the full suite is unchanged (892 passed, only the 2 pre-existing French-locale `toFormat` failures remain, which also fail with my change stashed). Only src/interval.js was modified.

Working on it. `src/impl/util.js` holds `isLeapYear(year)` (line 135), which is what `daysInMonth`/`daysInYear`/`conversions.js` use, so a wrong leap-year result around year 100 would break `plus`/`minus` across the 100 barrier through February. A subagent is fixing it and running the full suite; ETA ~8 min.

#4 still in progress: the leap-year helper in src/impl/util.js looks correct on inspection, so a diagnostic agent is empirically hunting the exact wrong `plus` result around the year-100/February boundary. ETA ~6 min.
#1 is fixed and verified (see my earlier reply).
#8: a subagent is fixing `DateTime#isInDST()` in src/datetime.js so it returns true for the whole 1974 US year-round DST period (America/New_York, 1974-01-06 through 1974-10-27). ETA ~8 min.

`Settings.defaultZone` returns `LocalZone.instance` — the getter is `return defaultZone || LocalZone.instance;` (src/settings.js:61-63). The `null` initial value is a deliberate placeholder to avoid loading-order issues, so a null internal `defaultZone` falls back to the system's local zone.
It returns the string `"[error]"` (site/demo/demo.js:12-15): the `catch` block logs the exception with `console.error(e)` and returns `"[error]"` immediately, so the `switch` below is never reached.

It concatenates them into one HTML string and writes it into the page: `examples.join("")` is appended to a header/paragraph/`<table>` opener (lines 80-85), and the whole string is assigned to `document.body.innerHTML` (line 87). Each element of `examples` is a `<tr class='example'>…</tr>` row built by `example()`, so the array becomes the body of the table. The array itself is left as-is (not cleared), and nothing is returned — `demo` returns `undefined`.
#11: a subagent is hunting the wrong unit conversion in src/duration.js (likely a bad entry in the casual/accurate conversion matrices) and will fix it. ETA ~10 min.

`"latn"` (Latin/ASCII digits). `digitRegex` does `numberingSystems[numberingSystem || "latn"]`, so an undefined/falsy `numberingSystem` falls back to the `latn` entry, whose pattern is `\d` (src/impl/digits.js:22, 74-76).

`defaultZone = null` (src/settings.js:49-55): the setter checks `if (!z)`, so any falsy value — empty string, null, undefined — resets the internal `defaultZone` to `null`, which makes the `defaultZone` getter fall back to `LocalZone.instance`. It does not call `normalizeZone` in that case.
#1 fixed and verified.

#4 still in progress: the leap-year helper in src/impl/util.js is correct as written, so a diagnostic agent is brute-forcing `plus`/`minus` around the year-100 February boundary to pin down the real divergence. ETA ~5 min.
#8 still in progress (DateTime#isInDST for the 1974 US year-round DST period). ETA ~5 min.

It's an abstract interface member: the base `Zone` class's `type` getter just `throw new ZoneIsAbstractError()` (src/zone.js:13-15). It's documented as `@abstract` and `@type {string}` — concrete subclasses (LocalZone → "local", IANAZone → "iana", FixedOffsetZone → "fixed", InvalidZone → "invalid") override it to return their type string. So calling it on a bare `Zone` instance throws rather than returning anything.

It returns a `FixedOffsetZone` built from the parsed offset: `zone = new FixedOffsetZone(matches.Z)` (src/impl/tokenParser.js:303-304). `matches.Z` is the offset in minutes produced by the `Z`/`ZZ`/`ZZZ` token, so the returned zone is a fixed-offset zone at that offset (the `z` token instead yields `IANAZone.create(matches.z)`, and neither gives `null`).

Hour 24 is valid only when the rest of the time is exactly zero: `validHour = integerBetween(hour, 0, 23) || (hour === 24 && minute === 0 && second === 0 && millisecond === 0)` (src/impl/conversions.js:141-143). So `24:00:00.000` is accepted (as end-of-day), while `24:00:01` or `24:30` are rejected as "unit out of range".

`'narrow'`, `'short'`, or `'techie'` — per the docstring on `Zone#formatOffset` (src/zone.js:48-58): "Accepts 'narrow', 'short', or 'techie'. Returning '+6', '+06:00', or '+0600' respectively". (In the base class the method is abstract and throws `ZoneIsAbstractError`; the concrete implementations in src/impl/util.js `formatOffset` throw a `RangeError` for any other value.)

#15 fixed and verified. `padStart` in src/impl/util.js now handles negative numbers (`"-" + ("" + -input).padStart(n, "0")`), so `DateTime.fromObject({ year: -100, ... }).toISODate()` gives `-0100-05-25`. The existing `[±YYYYY]` test still passes and no pre-existing test regressed.

#4 fixed and verified. Root cause was `objToLocalTS` in src/impl/util.js: it built the date with `Date.UTC` (year 99 → 1999) and then only shifted the year back by 1900, so day-overflow normalization happened in the 2000 timeline (a leap year) while year 100 is not — making every result on/after 0100-03-01 one day early (e.g. `DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({ days: 61 })` gave 0100-03-01 instead of 0100-03-02). It now re-sets year/month/day together: `d.setUTCFullYear(obj.year, obj.month - 1, obj.day)`. An exhaustive scan (years 90-110, ±1..100 days, months, years) went from 820 mismatches to 0, and the existing "across the 100 barrier" plus/minus tests still pass.

#11 fixed and verified. The conversion matrices in src/duration.js were missing three entries, so `quarters` conversions silently produced 0: `casualMatrix.years.quarters` (= 4), `casualMatrix.quarters.seconds` (= 91*24*60*60) and `accurateMatrix.years.quarters` (= 4) have been added. All 9x9 unit pairs now convert correctly (verified against the documented table in docs/math.md, both casual and longterm accuracy); test/duration is 114/114 green and no pre-existing test regressed.

#18 fixed and verified. `FixedOffsetZone#isValid` was hard-coded to `true`; it now returns `isNumber(this.fixed)`, so `FixedOffsetZone.instance("bogus").isValid === false` and a DateTime created in such a zone is invalid with reason "unsupported zone". Both target tests pass, all 5 test/zones suites are green, and no pre-existing test regressed.
